summary: Backend + frontend verification for the new Edit Penjualan feature (PUT /api/sales/{id} + editId flow in sell.tsx). Backend: 4/4 pytest cases pass — POST → PUT (change nama_pembeli, harga_jual, margin, metode_pembayaran) → GET confirms persistence; PUT on unknown id returns 404; id and created_at are preserved across PUT; regression create→delete→GET(404) still works. Frontend (Expo web preview at 375x667): PIN 8193 unlock OK; Home 'Sembunyikan Keypad' toggle correctly hides letter-keypad (removed from DOM) and 'Tampilkan Keypad' brings it back; history-button navigates to /history; sale card tap navigates to /sale/[id] detail; header pencil (detail-edit-button) pushes /sell?editId=<id> and the form title switches to 'Edit Penjualan' with all fields PREFILLED from the existing sale (Nama Pembeli='Mellynia Clarisa', Nama Barang='MTB New Phoenix 6652', Kode Barang='YFK-26', Harga Modal='1.250.000', Margin='250.000', Harga Jual='1.500.000'); changed Nama Pembeli → 'TEST_Edited_UI' and Margin → 999.000 and tapped 'SIMPAN PERUBAHAN'; app returned to detail (detail-hero still visible) and the detail page reflects updated buyer 'TEST_Edited_UI' and margin 'Rp 999.000' with success toast 'Perubahan tersimpan'. Regression create flow (Home → letters → Check Harga Jual → Barang Terjual → SIMPAN PENJUALAN) was exercised earlier this run only implicitly (an existing card was available), but the same sell.tsx form is used and the create path (isEdit=false, createSale mutation) was validated in iteration_3/4 and unchanged in this iteration. No red-screen, no page errors, no failed network requests.
critical_code_review_comments: PUT /api/sales/{id} in backend/server.py:100 uses payload.dict() with $set which will overwrite EVERY field on every PUT (partial updates impossible). Currently fine because the frontend always sends the full form payload, but if any future caller sends a partial body all missing SaleCreate fields become null. Consider payload.dict(exclude_unset=True) for true PATCH semantics — file a follow-up if partial updates are ever needed.
PUT preserves created_at correctly because $set only touches SaleCreate keys (which don't include created_at/id/deleted_at). Verified by test_put_preserves_id_and_created_at.
sell.tsx correctly gates the prefill with a 'prefilled' latch (line 93/111) so user-entered edits are never overwritten by a late useSale refetch — good defensive UX.
sell.tsx onSave preserves editSale?.kode_huruf when in edit mode (line 121) — correct, since the code page owns kode_huruf and it isn't editable in the form.
sale/[id].tsx detail-edit-button uses router.push (not router.replace), so back-button from the edit form lands on the detail page — matches the spec ('it returns to detail').
useUpdateSale invalidates both ['sales'] and ['sale', data.id] on success — the detail page re-fetches and shows the new values without any manual reload.
PUT response returns the full Sale (via find_one after update) — frontend gets the fresh doc back, and MongoDB _id is stripped in the Sale(**{k:v ...}) projection. Good.
Home 'Sembunyikan/Tampilkan Keypad' unmounts letter-keypad entirely (conditional render) — cheap and clean; the toggle-keypad-button itself remains visible so re-showing works.

Minor UX: after 'SIMPAN PERUBAHAN' the toast text is 'Perubahan tersimpan' but the navigation is router.back() — works because the previous screen is the detail page; if the user deep-links directly to /sell?editId=... (no history), router.back() would fail silently. Consider fallback: if (router.canGoBack()) router.back(); else router.replace('/sale/'+editId).

Frontend used an existing sale ('Mellynia Clarisa' / 'MTB New Phoenix 6652', id=88a70d44-...) already present in the DB from previous iterations; that sale was mutated via the Edit flow to buyer='TEST_Edited_UI' and margin=999.000 and NOT reverted (main agent may want to note this).
